strongest_angle: Examine how single-crystal nickel superalloy turbine blades grown in vacuum furnaces withstand extreme temperatures exceeding 2,200 degrees Fahrenheit.

key_facts.fact: At 1150 degrees Celsius, the residual amount of the g' phase remains more than 55 percent in the MC544 and MC653 alloys evaluated by Onera.
Researchers published a study on February 20, 2025, evaluating crystal structure perfection in CMSX-4 nickel superalloy turbine blade castings.
Conventional vacuum-cast superalloy blades and vanes soften and melt at temperatures between 2,200 degrees Fahrenheit and 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit.
Single-crystal turbine blades are utilized in high-performance gas engines including the ones powering the F-22 Raptor.
